jobDescription: The push notification service delivers messages to the mobile apps of the company's customers through several provider channels. The Backend Engineer operates the service in production: has deployed service changes to production through the deployment pipeline, holds a place on the on-call rota and has handled production incidents such as delivery backlogs or a provider outage, watches live delivery latency, and documents service boundaries. Load testing in staging supports the role but is not a substitute for production operation. The role sits in the platform group and works with the service's SRE pair, the mobile app teams and the provider account managers.
requirements: Has deployed service changes to production through the deployment pipeline.
Holds a place on the on-call rota and has handled production incidents such as delivery backlogs or provider outages.
Watches live delivery latency and records own responsibility boundaries for the service.
Develops provider adapters and the retry scheduler with load tests against a staging cluster.
Documents load-test findings, limitations and hand-over conditions for each release candidate.

evidence.text: Developed the provider adapters and the retry scheduler for the push notification service in the development environment, with the integration tests running against the providers' sandboxes.

Ran load tests against the staging cluster with synthetic traffic at up to 15k messages a second, recording the latency percentiles and the queue depth in the load-test report for each release candidate.

Deployments through the deployment pipeline, the on-call rota and production incident handling were owned by the service's SRE pair; my changes reached them through code review and the release candidate tag, and I held no deployment rights.

Wrote the runbook drafts for the retry scheduler and the hand-over notes for each release candidate, listing the staging cluster's differences from the customer-facing cluster and the open items for SRE.
About two years on the notification service covered adapter development, the retry scheduler, staging load tests, runbook drafts and hand-over notes.
Work sample: the load-test report for release candidate twelve with the staging cluster's run identifiers, and the runbook draft for the retry scheduler.

Recruiter screen: candidate said she had 'deployed the retry scheduler to prod' and 'been paged for delivery backlogs'; asked for an example, she described a staging load test that filled the queue and said SRE 'took the real ones'.

Hiring manager pre-read: the candidate's GitHub profile README says she 'runs a notification service at 40k messages a second in production'; the head of platform wants an engineer who has deployed to production and handled incidents on call, so the packet must say which environment each item happened in.

propositions.rationale: The resume and the load-test report document the development work and the staging tests.

propositions.text: The candidate wrote the runbook drafts and the hand-over notes for each release candidate, listing the staging cluster's differences and the open items for SRE.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the runbook draft document the artefacts.

propositions.text: The candidate deployed service changes to production, ran the service at 40k messages a second, held a place on the on-call rota and handled production incidents such as delivery backlogs.
propositions.rationale: The resume places the candidate's work in the development environment and the staging cluster and deployments, on-call and incident handling with the SRE pair; her screen example was a staging load test.

gold.expectedGap: The materials document development-environment work and staging load tests; they do not document the candidate deploying to production, holding an on-call place or handling a production incident.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the environment the resume names: development environment and staging cluster; deployments, on-call and production incidents belonged to the SRE pair.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate has ever held deployment rights or an on-call place for the service, and which production incident she handled.
